title: NO GIANT TOO GREAT FOR GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Next we turned and went up along the road toward Bashan, and Og king of Bashan with his whole army marched out to meet us in battle at Edrei. The Lord said to me, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have delivered him into your hands, along with his whole army and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon." - Deut 3:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Israel now faced Og, king of Bashan, a formidable foe who came out with his whole army. Og was famous for his size and strength — a giant of a king ruling a land of fortified cities. If anyone was going to intimidate God's people, it was Og. Yet God's first word to Moses was, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have delivered him into your hands." Once again, before the battle even began, God spoke of the victory as already secured.

Notice how God grounds their courage in what He had already done: "Do to him what you did to Sihon." God reminded them of the recent victory to build their faith for the new challenge. This is how God often strengthens us — by calling to mind His past faithfulness so we can face present fears. The God who gave victory yesterday is the same God we trust today.

Fear tends to magnify our giants. Og was genuinely powerful, and it would have been easy for Israel to focus on his strength and tremble. But God calls His people to focus not on the size of the giant but on the greatness of God. The giant that terrifies us is small before the Lord.

Whatever "Og" you are facing — a challenge that towers over you, a fear that seems unbeatable — hear God's word: "Do not be afraid." Remember how He has helped you before, and trust Him for what lies ahead. No giant is too great for God. In Christ, we face our battles knowing the One who has already overcome the greatest enemies of sin and death goes with us (1 Cor 15:57). Take courage.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "giant" is towering over you and stirring up fear?
2. How can remembering God's past faithfulness build your courage now?
3. What does it mean to focus on God's greatness rather than the giant's size?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Mighty God, when giants tower over me and fear takes hold, remind me of Your past faithfulness and speak Your word: "Do not be afraid." Help me trust Your greatness, knowing Christ has overcome the greatest enemies. Amen.
